title: Tia Finds Balance
moral: Helping others is good, but taking care of your own needs is important too.

scenes.summary: Tia is a kind bird who loves helping others but does too much.
scenes.text:
Tia the Bird Who Carried Everyone’s Work

In a bright forest full of singing birds, lived a kind little bird named Tia.

Tia loved helping others.

She was always ready to lend a wing.

But there was one problem…

Tia helped too much.

scenes.summary: Tia keeps taking on others' work and becomes overwhelmed.
scenes.text:
“Can you carry my twigs?” asked Roro the Robin.

“Sure!” said Tia.

“Can you gather my leaves?” asked Pipi the Parrot.

“Of course!” said Tia.

Soon, Tia was doing everyone’s work.
scenes.image_prompt: bird carrying many twigs and leaves for others looking busy, cartoon style

scenes.summary: Tia becomes exhausted and realizes she is falling behind.
scenes.text:
Tia flew here and there.

Carrying twigs…

Collecting leaves…

Helping everyone.

But soon, she felt very tired.

“I can’t keep up,” she said.

One day, Tia needed to build her own nest.

But she hadn’t started.

“I helped everyone,” she said,

“but I forgot my own work.”
scenes.image_prompt: tired bird with many tasks looking worried about unfinished nest, cartoon scene

scenes.summary: Omi advises Tia to balance helping others with her own needs.
scenes.text:
Just then, Omi the Owl flew down.

“Why are you worried?” he asked.

“I helped too much,” Tia said.

“And now I’m behind.”

Omi nodded.

“Helping is good,” he said,

“but you must also help yourself.”
scenes.image_prompt: wise owl advising tired bird in forest, warm cartoon style

scenes.summary: Tia learns to prioritize her work and help others afterward.
scenes.text:
Tia thought for a moment.

“You’re right,” she said.

The next day, when friends asked for help—

“I’ll help after I finish my work,” she said kindly.

Tia built her nest first.

Then she helped her friends.

She felt happy and strong.

“This is much better!” she chirped.

Helping others is good,

but don’t forget your own needs.

Balance is important.

The End

story:
Tia the Bird Who Carried Everyone’s Work

In a bright forest full of singing birds, lived a kind little bird named Tia.

Tia loved helping others.

She was always ready to lend a wing.

But there was one problem…

Tia helped too much.

“Can you carry my twigs?” asked Roro the Robin.

“Sure!” said Tia.

“Can you gather my leaves?” asked Pipi the Parrot.

“Of course!” said Tia.

Soon, Tia was doing everyone’s work.

Tia flew here and there.

Carrying twigs…

Collecting leaves…

Helping everyone.

But soon, she felt very tired.

“I can’t keep up,” she said.

One day, Tia needed to build her own nest.

But she hadn’t started.

“I helped everyone,” she said,

“but I forgot my own work.”

Just then, Omi the Owl flew down.

“Why are you worried?” he asked.

“I helped too much,” Tia said.

“And now I’m behind.”

Omi nodded.

“Helping is good,” he said,

“but you must also help yourself.”

Tia thought for a moment.

“You’re right,” she said.

The next day, when friends asked for help—

“I’ll help after I finish my work,” she said kindly.

Tia built her nest first.

Then she helped her friends.

She felt happy and strong.

“This is much better!” she chirped.

Helping others is good,

but don’t forget your own needs.

Balance is important.

The End
